translations.text: For I know that there can be no justice among people without a true standard, especially among a multitude with no one to guide them in equality.
They will be like a ship tossed to and fro, whose course you cannot guide from one shore of the sea to the other, not to mention the open sea.
Some deceive because of bodily [?]; others grumble because of these same circumstances. Some want to steal, or indeed do steal; others find fault.

Some engage in falsehoods; others have an alien heart. Some want pleasure for themselves alone; others want to find their own comfort, whether they are sick or well. For this is what happens in many communities: they say that they live in community with one another, but they do not do so uprightly.
No one who truly lives in community will ever seek comfort for themselves alone and abandon any of those who share communal life with them.
Perfect communal life means living in this same equality. And woe to those who live in these places at any time if they follow other ways that show favoritism.

For this reason, I decree that these three kinds of food should always be kept in these places for those among us who are sick: fish sauce; cheese, however they want it, whether dried or salted; and eggs, whether salted or whether they want to [?] them in a boiling pot, or however they want them.

But no one among us, whether male or female, is ever to eat such things except those who are genuinely sick and have been recognized as such by all the faithful brothers, and especially by the fathers of these places at any time, who will give an account to God for those gathered in them.
No one is to eat such things anywhere except in the place set aside for the sick alone,
where they ask for a little wine.
